figures.name: a fish swimming left, with a forked tail and fins
figures.how: I made the body a diamond from the two large triangles and found the forked tail by setting the square as a stem with the two small triangles notched into a V behind it; the fins took three tries before the shape read as a fish.
figures.seen_before: unsure: diamond-bodied tangram fish are common, but I did not copy a specific one

figures.name: a cat sitting, seen from the side, tail raised
figures.how: Two large triangles make a sloping seated body, the square set on the back is the head with the small triangles as ears, and I moved the parallelogram from the ground to an upright tail at the back after looking.
figures.seen_before: yes: the seated tangram cat with a square head and triangle ears is a well-known traditional figure

figures.name: an arrow pointing up
figures.how: I meant it as a house (a roof of both large triangles over a square wall of the five small pieces tiled on a root-2 grid), but the silhouette reads as an up arrow, so that is what I am calling it.
figures.seen_before: unsure: the arrow/house shape is a common outline, not a specific tangram figure I remember
